insight.title: Why a Noisy Room Helps You Focus
insight.subtitle: Why background distractions actually make your brain sharper

sections.text: You sit in a silent room to focus, yet your mind feels louder than ever. We often assume that removing every distraction is the key to clarity, but silence can be surprisingly heavy.

Renaissance workshops and Enlightenment coffee houses were famously loud. Science confirms that this “stochastic resonance”—where background noise helps the brain detect weak signals—was a key driver of the creative breakthroughs in those eras.

This noise acts as a sensory anchor. It gives your peripheral awareness just enough to do, preventing your mind from wandering toward disruptive internal thoughts or the constant urge to check your phone.
Try this today: The next time you feel distracted today, embrace the background noise instead of fighting it.
Focus isn't found by removing the world, but by finding the right frequency to tune into.
